behavior: The callable first invokes GetBusinessDayReconciliationAsync for sales, expenses and shift discrepancy, then reloads BusinessDay by ID. It obtains the Cairo [start,end) UTC interval for that day, selects EmployeeLedgerEntries by CreatedAtUtc only, and sums DailyWage/Overtime credits and Advance/Withdrawal debits across all employees. It separately selects shifts by BusinessDate and distinct OpenedByUserId names. It returns a read-only DailySummaryDto containing day ID/date, sales, expenses, shortage/overage, the four ledger totals, and cashier names. There is no per-request transaction or snapshot across the reconciliation, business-day reload, ledger and shift/name reads.

conclusions: No independent material calculation defect identified in the four ledger totals: selected types, credit/debit sides, and Cairo timestamp range match the DTO contract and current writers inspected.

The query is calendar-date scoped rather than businessDayId scoped because EmployeeLedgerEntryEntity has no BusinessDayId; current writer timestamps and comments support that date-based contract. If multiple distinct BusinessDay IDs for one date are allowed and expected to have separate ledger summaries, each summary will repeat same-day employee entries and cashier names. This reuses the prior conditional date-vs-ID cohort observation; not a new finding.

The report reads are non-snapshot and could combine values across concurrent updates; no database isolation/outcome is established. Existing source comments describe a printable end-of-day sheet, but no direct endpoint test exists.
The DTO intentionally omits Salary, ExtraShift, Settlement and PayrollSettlement; this is a scoped daily summary, not a total employee-obligation/payroll report. No owner-policy gap is asserted.
